details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for severe storms capable of mainly severe wind gusts, potentially up to 70-80 mph, is expected to increase across the discussion area late this afternoon into evening. An additional watch is possible to the east/southeast of the recently issued severe thunderstorm watch 584 in effect across southeast Colorado

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Thunderstorms have developed along the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and adjacent Raton Mesa with a deepening cumulus field noted along a warm front from southwest KS into the OK and TX Panhandles. The 18Z DDC and AMA soundings modified for current surface conditions exhibit steep environmental lapse rates (especially in the low levels) with MLCAPE of 1500-2500 J/kg. Continued daytime heating should allow for further air mass destabilization with the strongest instability forecast north of the front from far southeast CO into southwest KS. Latest CAM guidance suggests the storms developing along the Sangre de Cristo Mountains will gradually grow upscale into one or multiple clusters later this afternoon into evening while moving/developing east into the High Plains. The recently issued severe thunderstorm watch 584 accounts for the large hail and severe wind gust potential with that regime. Additional storms will also be possible along the surface boundary from the northern TX into OK Panhandles and southwest KS, with some model signal for the separate regimes to merge across southwest KS this evening. Severe wind gusts, potentially up to 70-80 mph, appear to be the primary hazard with the latter regime, and convective trends are being monitored for an additional severe thunderstorm watch

details.label: Summary
details.text: The potential for severe storms capable of large hail and severe wind gusts is expected to increase this afternoon into evening. A severe thunderstorm watch is possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Visible satellite imagery and lightning data indicate thunderstorms developing over the central Rockies, including the CO Front Range, with additional storms noted over central into northeast WY, and the far northwest NE Panhandle. More widespread cloud cover has slowed daytime heating across portions of the adjacent High Plains, where latest objective analysis indicates lingering convective inhibition. However, continued daytime heating should allow the cap to weaken, thereby allowing storms to advance into the High Plains, amidst a steep lapse rate environment featuring MLCAPE of 1000-1500 J/kg. When coupled with 30-40 kt of deep-layer shear, the setup will support multicell and some supercell storm modes capable of mainly large hail initially. Latest CAM guidance continues to suggest that storms will grow upscale into clusters this evening with an associated increase in severe wind gust potential
